newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle markets at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle markets at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet near midday, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
This week's sales at $72.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week, cleared out most feedlot showlists, they said.

Prices were lifted by tight supplies of the type of cattle that will grade choice, firm packer demand to meet beef orders for retail features before Thanksgiving and higher boxed beef prices, market sources said.
The choice, heavyweight beef price Thursday at $112.48 was up $3.29 from a week ago, according to USDA figures.

By Thursday, 88,700 head had sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area for the week to date, including 14,100 formulated cattle, 100 previously contracted to be shipped this week and 1,500 head or 41 loads of CME cattle delivered to area packing plants, USDA reported.
In Kansas, sales were confirmed for the week on 80,800 including 16,800 head or about 21 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Slaughter Monday will be curbed by the Veterans Day holiday.
An IBP Inc spokesman said its plants at Amarillo, Texas; Emporia, Kan.; and West Point, Neb. would be closed.
A spokesman for the National Beef Packing Co. unit of Farmland Industries Inc said its Liberal, Kan.; plant also will be closed.
Other comapny officials with key beef packing companies were unavailable for comment.
